prize_parts.citation: For the invention and development of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, enabling frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: The optical lattice clock rests on one clean piece of atomic-structure physics: at the magic wavelength the light shifts of the two clock states cancel, so thousands of neutral atoms can be held without Doppler or recoil shifts while a very narrow transition is interrogated. That idea, attributed to Katori, together with the Sr lattice clock work at Tokyo and at JILA under Ye, has taken fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 range. The achievement is a discovery-and-invention in the sense of the statutes, it is reproduced by independent laboratories on several continents and in several species, and it already delivers new physics: tests of fundamental constants and of relativity, relativistic geodesy, and a route to a redefinition of the second. The credit is also the cleanest on the shortlist: two names, with a concept originator and a performance and many-body-control leader. The 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured the comb and ion control that this builds on, not the lattice concept, so there is no real duplication.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that frequency metrology is arguably an evolutionary sequence (combs, single-ion clocks, lattice clocks) in which the lattice step could be seen as a refinement, and that lattice-clock credit is wider than two names: Ye's results depend on collaborators at JILA and NIST, ytterbium lattice clocks at NIST and elsewhere, the original Sr demonstrations by Takamoto and colleagues, and SYRTE and PTB work. The redefinition of the second has not happened, so some colleagues may regard the full payoff as still pending. Finally, I am a theoretical atomic physicist, and my enthusiasm for the atomic-physics elegance may be overweighting this relative to the breadth of impact of the condensed-matter candidates.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks DMFT first for its consequential theory-to-materials impact and puts optical lattice clocks only eighth, saying the clock is outside his core field and weighing it with caution.
responses.response: I accept that DMFT is a mature, widely used and consequential framework, and I ranked it sixth for that reason. But I would not read the low rank as a judgement on the clock's merit, because he himself calls it a clear and important measurement advance with clean credit. DMFT is a method whose credit is shared with Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and others who are not on the credited list, so a trio is imperfect, whereas the clock candidate yields a defensible two-person allocation and a concrete, independently verified measurement result. I would also resist treating methodological breadth in condensed matter as the same thing as a discovery that can be pointed to and tested.

responses.point: Johansson places circuit QED first as close to decisive for superconducting quantum technology and notes both the 2025 prize overlap and his own connections to that community.
responses.response: I agree that circuit QED is original and has had very large impact, and I ranked it third. My qualification is the one he raises: the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is close enough in context that a second circuit award so soon could look repetitive, and the credit question around Girvin and the transmon inventors is real. I respect his disclosure of connections, but it is a reason to discount that first place somewhat in the discussion. I do not see a comparable timing problem for lattice clocks, which he himself ranks second and calls timely and mature.

responses.point: Pearce ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first for its broad, original impact and a fair theory-plus-experiment split, while accepting that the superconductivity is still debated, and puts the lattice clock second.
responses.response: I share the view that the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the 2018 experiments created a major field, and I ranked it fourth. Our disagreement is on maturity. Roughly eight years after the experiments, the origin of the superconductivity and of several correlated and fractional Chern states is unsettled, and experimental credit is shared with Cao, Dean, Young, Efetov and others. I would not call the interpretation stable. The clock result is in contrast a settled measurement, tested by independent comparison, so I would prefer to let twisted bilayer graphene mature one or two more years.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks the clock first but asks whether the single-ion clock lineage and frequency-comb metrology, honoured in 2005 and 2012, must be acknowledged in the citation.
responses.response: I think the citation should be framed around the magic-wavelength lattice and the many-atom interrogation so that it is plainly distinct from the earlier prizes, with no wording that implies the comb or ion control is being re-awarded. The earlier work is a tool the lattice clock uses, not the idea being recognised, so I do not think it forces extra names.

uncertainties: Exact first-demonstration attribution among strontium, ytterbium and other lattice clocks, and how much weight Takamoto, Hong, Ludlow and the NIST and SYRTE groups deserve relative to the two credited names, cannot be settled from the materials here.
Whether a redefinition of the second should be awaited, or is not needed, before honouring the lattice clock.

Whether the committee would pair the clock with a second distinct achievement; with a three-person cap, a second part could only carry one name from B030 or B042, which I do not consider a fair split.
statement.conflict_note: For the preferred B012 configuration (Katori, Ye) no specific conflict is apparent from my profile. For disclosure only: my profile documents collaboration with Anne L'Huillier, with the Lund attosecond group and with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zürich, so I would flag possible sensitivity if candidates tied to those groups were discussed; Wallraff in B005 is at ETH Zürich, though no relationship with him is documented. I make no other connection claim.
